subject: History
chapter: Colonialism and the Countryside: Exploring Official Archives
central_question: How did colonial revenue systems transform rural Bengal, the Rajmahal hills and the Deccan, and how should historians read official archives alongside peasant resistance?
in_scope_units: Permanent Settlement, Burdwan auction and revenue default.
Jotedars, zamindars, fictitious sales and the Fifth Report.
Paharia livelihoods and Company pacification in the Rajmahal hills.
Ryotwari revenue assessment in the Bombay Deccan.
Peasant debt, moneylenders and the burning of account books.
The American Civil War, cotton boom and collapse of credit.
The Deccan Riots Commission and the interpretation of official archives.
banned_topics: Mughal revenue administration under the Ain-i Akbari, treated in the previous chapter.
The military and political history of the Revolt of 1857, treated in the next chapter.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Permanent Settlement made zamindars secure private owners who always improved agriculture.
known_pitfalls.correction: High rigid revenue, low prices, collection problems and auctions destabilised many estates, while investment did not follow automatically.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Rajmahal hills were empty until Santhals cleared them.
known_pitfalls.correction: Paharias and other communities already used the forests through shifting cultivation, hunting, gathering and seasonal mobility.

known_pitfalls.claim: Official reports reproduce peasant experience without mediation.
known_pitfalls.correction: Officials selected questions, translated testimony and wrote for administrative purposes, so the records must be critically corroborated.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 6 on auctions after Permanent Settlement.

NCERT Exercise 8 on the American Civil War and ryots.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with questions 1-5 in the 100-150 word section, essay questions 6-9, Map work 10 and Projects 11-12.
